step_by_step_reasoning:
1. Identify all visual nodes with distinct icons: Users (UserConsumerWeb), CloudFront, EC2 (running Varnish), EKS, ECR, Aurora, ElastiCache, and S3.
2. Trace arrows visually on the whiteboard:
- Users -> CloudFront
- CloudFront -> EC2
- CloudFront -> S3
- EC2 -> EKS
- EKS -> ECR
- EKS -> Aurora
- EKS -> ElastiCache
- EKS -> S3 (via S3FUSE)
3. Sequence the flows starting from user requests into CloudFront and down through caching, compute, container registry, storage, and databases.

graph.name: Love Bonito E-Commerce Architecture on AWS
graph.notes: Architecture showing Magento e-commerce deployment with CloudFront, EC2 Varnish cache, EKS, ECR, S3 via S3FUSE, Aurora MySQL, and ElastiCache Redis.

nodes.name: USERS
nodes.notes: End users accessing the web application

nodes.name: EKS

nodes.name: ECR

nodes.name: AURORA

nodes.name: ELASTICACHE

edges.notes: CloudFront routes traffic to Varnish on EC2
Varnish forwards uncached requests to EKS
EKS caches data in ElastiCache Redis
CloudFront delivers static content directly from S3
